\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Basis}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Hermite.Basis
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Hermite.Basis}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Hermite functions belong to finite-order spaces]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_eval_gaussian, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, multi-index $\alpha:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$, and
exponent $p\in[0,\infty]$ with $p\ne\infty$, the Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$
belongs to $L^p$ for the product of $n$ standard Gaussian measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hermite functions are square integrable]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp}
\difficulty{2}
For every natural number $n$ and multi-index $\alpha:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$, the
Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$ belongs to $L^2$ for the product of $n$ standard
Gaussian measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Hermite functions in the $L^2$ space]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two}
For a natural number $n$ and a multi-index $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb N$, define
the corresponding element of the Gaussian $L^2$ space as the $L^2$ equivalence class of
the Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite polynomial in Gaussian $L^2$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp_hermite}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp_hermite}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $\alpha:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$. Under the
product standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, the image in $L^2$ of the
multivariate Hermite polynomial indexed by $\alpha$ is the $L^2$ class of its Hermite
function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Gaussian polynomials in the Hermite span]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp_mem_span_hermiteL2}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp_mem_span_hermiteL2}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp_hermite, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.multivariateHermitePolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.span_multivariateHermitePolynomial_eq_top}
\difficulty{4}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$ and every real polynomial $P$ in $n$ variables, the element of
Gaussian $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ represented by $P$ belongs to the real linear span of the
multivariate Hermite functions.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Inner product of Gaussian $L^2$ classes]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_toLp_eq_integral_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_toLp_eq_integral_mul}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and functions $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that belong to
$L^2$ for standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$, the inner product of their $L^2$ classes
is $\int f(x)g(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and every pair of multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb
N^n$, the inner product in Gaussian $L^2(\mathbb R^n)$ of their normalized multivariate
Hermite functions is $1$ if $\alpha=\beta$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For any dimension $n$ and multi-indices $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite
coefficient of the Hermite function $H_\alpha$ at $\beta$ is $1$ if $\alpha=\beta$ and
$0$ otherwise.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite coefficients of finite sums]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_finset_sum_hermiteFunction}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_finset_sum_hermiteFunction}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integral_hermiteFunction_mul}
\difficulty{4}
For any dimension $n$, finite index set $s$, real coefficients $c_i$, multi-indices
$a_i\in\mathbb N^n$, and multi-index $\beta\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient at
$\beta$ of the function $x\mapsto\sum_{i\in s}c_i H_{a_i}(x)$ is $\sum_{i\in s} c_i$
when $a_i=\beta$ and $0$ otherwise; equivalently, it is $\sum_{i\in
s}\mathbf{1}_{a_i=\beta}c_i$, where $H_\alpha$ denotes the multivariate Hermite
function.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Orthonormality of Hermite functions]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2_orthonormal}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2_orthonormal}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_hermiteL2}
\difficulty{1}
For every dimension $n$, the multivariate normalized Hermite functions form an
orthonormal family in $L^2(\bbr^n,\gamma_n)$, where $\gamma_n$ is the product of $n$
standard Gaussian probability measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Density of Hermite polynomials]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2_dense}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2_dense}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussianPolynomialLp_mem_span_hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.gaussian_polynomial_dense, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.memLp_eval_gaussian}
\difficulty{4}
For every dimension $n$, the linear span in $L^2(\bbr^n,\gamma_n)$ of the multivariate
normalized Hermite functions is dense, where $\gamma_n$ is the product of $n$ standard
Gaussian probability measures.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Hermite Hilbert basis]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis}
\statementsource{boolean-ch11-gaussian-invariance}{pdf-8b2c50cf9621-p012-b001}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2_dense, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2_orthonormal}
For a natural number $n$, the Hermite functions indexed by multi-indices in
$\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\mathbb N$ form a Hilbert basis of the real Gaussian $L^2$ space on
$\mathbb R^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite basis vectors]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis_apply}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis_apply}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and multi-index $\alpha:\{1,\ldots,n\}\to\mathbb N$, the
Hilbert basis vector indexed by $\alpha$ is the $L^2$ equivalence class of the Hermite
function indexed by $\alpha$, with respect to the product of $n$ standard Gaussian
measures.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite coefficient as an inner product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_hermiteL2_toLp}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_hermiteL2_toLp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_toLp_eq_integral_mul}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, and every
function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that belongs to $L^2$ for standard Gaussian measure
on $\mathbb R^n$, the inner product of its $L^2$ class with the normalized multivariate
Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$ equals $\int f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$, where
$H_\alpha$ denotes that Hermite function and $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure on
$\mathbb R^n$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite coefficient as an inner product]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_toLp_hermiteL2}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_toLp_hermiteL2}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_hermiteL2_toLp}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that belongs to
$L^2$ for standard Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$, and every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb
N^n$, the inner product of the $L^2$ class of $f$ with the normalized multivariate
Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$ equals $\int f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$, where
$H_\alpha$ denotes that Hermite function.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that is square-integrable for the product $\gamma_n$ of $n$ standard Gaussian measures, and every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the coefficient of the $L^2$ class of $f$ at the Hermite Hilbert basis vector indexed by $\alpha$ equals $\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$, where $H_\alpha$ is the corresponding Hermite function.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that is square-integrable for the product $\gamma_n$ of $n$ standard Gaussian measures, and every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the coefficient of the $L^2$ class of $f$ at the Hermite Hilbert basis vector indexed by $\alpha$ equals $\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$, where $H_\alpha$ is the corresponding Hermite function.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniqueness of Hermite coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_expansion_unique}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_expansion_unique}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_hermiteL2, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_hermiteL2_toLp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian
measures on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to
$L^2(\gamma_n)$. If a family of real coefficients $(c_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}$
has its Hermite series converge in $L^2(\gamma_n)$ to $f$, then for every
$\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, $c_\alpha=\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$,
where $H_\alpha$ is the multivariate Hermite function indexed by $\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The zero-order Hermite coefficient]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_zero}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_zero}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable
with respect to the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure. The Hermite coefficient
of $f$ at the zero multi-index equals the Gaussian integral $\int_{\mathbb R^n}
f\,d\gamma^{\otimes n}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ be square-integrable
with respect to the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure. Then the squared Hermite
coefficients of $f$ are summable over all multi-indices $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$; that is,
$\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}(\widehat f(\alpha))^2<\infty$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f,g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ belong to $L^2$ for
the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures. Then
\[
\int f(x)g(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^n}\widehat f(\alpha)\widehat
g(\alpha),
\]
where $\gamma_n$ is that product measure and $\widehat f(\alpha)=\int
f(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$ and $\widehat g(\alpha)=\int
g(x)H_\alpha(x)\,d\gamma_n(x)$ are the coefficients against the normalized multivariate
Hermite polynomials $H_\alpha$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Variance from Hermite coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.variance_eq_hermite}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.variance_eq_hermite}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sq_summable, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_zero, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_plancherel, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability
measures on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to
$L^2(\gamma_n)$. For each multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, let $c_\alpha$ be the
integral of $f$ against the corresponding normalized multivariate Hermite polynomial.
Then
\[
\operatorname{Var}_{\gamma_n}(f)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n,\,\alpha\ne0}c_\alpha^2.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Scalar multiplication of Hermite coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_const_mul}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_const_mul}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff}
\difficulty{1}
For any dimension $n$, real scalar $c$, function $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$, and
multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient of $cf$ at $\alpha$ equals
$c$ times the Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite coefficients of a difference]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sub}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sub}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteFunction_memLp_two}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f,g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ both be
square-integrable with respect to the $n$-dimensional standard Gaussian measure. For
every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Hermite coefficient of $f-g$ at $\alpha$
is the Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$ minus that of $g$ at $\alpha$.
\end{lemma}

\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ have finite second
moment under the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures. For every
multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the absolute value of the Hermite coefficient of $f$
indexed by $\alpha$ is at most the $L^2$ norm of $f$ under that product Gaussian
measure.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Continuity of Hermite coefficients in $L^2$]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_hermiteCoeff_of_eLpNorm_sub_tendsto}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.tendsto_hermiteCoeff_of_eLpNorm_sub_tendsto}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.abs_hermiteCoeff_le_eLpNorm_toReal, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff_sub}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge0$, let $(u_i)_{i\in\iota}$ and $f$ be real-valued functions on $\mathbb R^n$,
and let $\ell$ be a filter on $\iota$. Suppose $f$ is square-integrable under standard
Gaussian measure $\gamma_n$, the functions $u_i$ are square-integrable for all $i$ in
some set belonging to $\ell$, and $\|u_i-f\|_{L^2(\gamma_n)}\to0$ along $\ell$. Then,
for every multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, the Gaussian Hermite coefficient of $u_i$
at $\alpha$ tends along $\ell$ to the Gaussian Hermite coefficient of $f$ at $\alpha$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Realization of square-summable Hermite coefficients]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_memLp_hermiteCoeff}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.exists_memLp_hermiteCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteHilbertBasis_repr_toLp}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, and let $c$ assign a real number $c_\alpha$ to each
multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$. If $\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n} c_\alpha^2$
converges, then there is a function $g\colon\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ that belongs to
$L^2$ for the product standard Gaussian measure and whose Hermite coefficient at every
multi-index $\alpha$ is $c_\alpha$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Hermite coefficients and the Gaussian $L^2$ norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_two_eq_sqrt_hermiteCoeff}
\label{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.eLpNorm_two_eq_sqrt_hermiteCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermiteCoeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.hermite_plancherel, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.inner_toLp_eq_integral_mul}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be the product of $n$ standard Gaussian probability measures
on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R$ belong to $L^2(\gamma_n)$. If
$c_\alpha$ denotes the coefficient of $f$ against the normalized multivariate Hermite
polynomial indexed by $\alpha\in\mathbb N^n$, then
\[\|f\|_{L^2(\gamma_n)}=\sqrt{\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^n}c_\alpha^2}.\]
\end{lemma}
